content_units: You already have a strong base for   Customer Success Operations  : customer support operations experience, workflow exposure, stakeholder handling, and basic SQL. For a   9-month pivot in Dublin   targeting   €55k–€68k  , the most realistic route is to position yourself for   CS Ops Analyst / Revenue Ops–adjacent / Support-to-CS Operations hybrid roles   rather than senior strategy-only roles.
- Dublin hiring typically favors candidates with   CRM + reporting + process improvement + cross-functional execution
- Your support operations background is highly transferable if reframed around   retention, onboarding, customer lifecycle, tooling, and metrics
- The salary target is realistic for   mid-level operations roles   if you can show stronger tooling and business metrics within 9 months
Month 1-2   Define target role family   Shortlist titles; review 40-60 Dublin job posts; map recurring skills; rewrite LinkedIn headline   Target-role list + keyword bank
Month 2-3   Close core tooling gaps   Improve SQL; learn Excel/Sheets analysis; build CRM knowledge in Salesforce or HubSpot; learn CS metrics   2 mini-projects + skills section update
Month 3-5   Build ops portfolio   Create churn/cohort dashboard mockups; onboarding funnel analysis; support-to-CS handoff workflow; KPI reporting pack   3 portfolio artifacts
Month 5-6   Reposition market profile   Rewrite CV around outcomes; add quantified bullets; optimize LinkedIn; prepare achievement stories   New CV + LinkedIn + interview bank
Month 6-8   Start focused applications   Apply to Dublin roles weekly; prioritize SaaS and tech-enabled services; tailor CV by title cluster   30-50 quality applications
Month 7-9   Convert interviews to offers   Practice metrics-based answers; prep case studies; prepare salary pitch; refine storytelling for CS Ops   Interview-ready narrative + offer conversations
Prioritize these titles on LinkedIn, Indeed, IrishJobs, and company career pages:
-   Business Operations Analyst   with customer-facing lifecycle scope
-   Most realistic now:   Customer Operations Analyst, Support Operations Analyst, CS Operations Specialist
-   Good stretch roles:   Customer Success Operations Analyst, Revenue Operations Analyst
-   Useful alternatives if market is tight:   CRM Analyst, Customer Experience Analyst, Lifecycle Operations Analyst
To be credible for CS Ops in Dublin, you should strengthen these areas:
- Salesforce is the most valuable signal
- HubSpot is also useful, especially for SMB/SaaS employers
- Learn: accounts, contacts, opportunities, customer health inputs, workflow automation, reporting
You need to confidently talk about:
You do not need advanced data engineering.
- Excel / Google Sheets at advanced level
Learn how to frame your work in terms of:
You need examples showing you influenced teams without formal authority.
Focus only on what improves hiring odds fastest:
Option 1:   SQL + Salesforce + CS metrics     Highest ROI for target roles   Best hiring signal
Option 2:   Excel/Sheets + dashboarding     Helps with analyst-style interviews   Strong portfolio value
Option 3:   Customer success fundamentals     Helps with vocabulary and role framing   Important but secondary to tooling
Option 4:   HubSpot CRM basics     Good backup signal for growth-stage firms   Easier than Salesforce to demonstrate
Positioning Your Support Background for CS Operations
Your old story may sound like: “I handled support operations and some reporting.”
Your new story should sound like:
- “I improved customer lifecycle operations by using data to identify patterns, streamline workflows, and improve service outcomes.”
- “My background in support operations gives me direct visibility into customer friction, adoption blockers, and process gaps that affect retention.”
- “I am moving into Customer Success Operations because I want to work upstream on customer health, process design, reporting, and cross-functional execution.”
How to rewrite your CV bullets
- Improved ticket routing workflow across X queues, reducing response delays and improving SLA adherence by X%
- Built recurring support performance reports using SQL and spreadsheets, enabling leaders to spot volume trends and staffing gaps
- Identified top customer issue categories and escalated root causes to product/operations teams, contributing to lower repeat contacts
- Standardized case handling/process documentation, improving agent consistency and reducing onboarding time for new team members
- Partnered with customer-facing teams to improve escalation handling for high-risk accounts, supporting retention and customer satisfaction
- Used SQL to segment case trends by issue type, region, or account tier to guide operational decisions
What hiring managers need to hear
Translate your experience into these themes:
Avoid sounding like a pure front-line support candidate. Emphasize:
Customer Operations Analyst transitioning into Customer Success Operations   6 years in support operations   SQL, reporting, process improvement, customer lifecycle

Operations-focused customer professional with 6 years of experience in support operations, process improvement, reporting, and cross-functional coordination. Experienced in using data and workflow analysis to improve service delivery and identify customer friction points. Now targeting Customer Success Operations roles in Dublin, with growing capability in SQL, CRM reporting, lifecycle metrics, and operational optimization.
Interview Positioning for Customer Success Operations
-   Where I come from:   6 years in customer support operations
-   What I learned:   customer pain points, service processes, reporting, operational bottlenecks
-   Why this pivot makes sense:   CS Ops lets you solve customer problems at scale
-   Why I can do it now:   you already have operations experience and are adding CRM, metrics, and stronger analytics
- “Support operations gave me a close view of where customers get stuck; CS Ops is the natural next step because it lets me improve those patterns systematically.”
- “I’m strongest where customer impact meets process and data.”
- “I’m not pivoting away from customer work; I’m moving closer to the operational levers that improve retention and customer outcomes.”
Questions you should be ready for
- Because you want to move from reactive issue management to proactive lifecycle and retention support
Why should we hire you over someone already in CS Ops?
- You bring deep customer friction insight, operational discipline, and hands-on exposure to the issues that affect adoption and retention
How do you handle skill gaps?
- Show a concrete plan: SQL practice, CRM training, dashboard projects, job-post-based learning roadmap
Tell me about a process improvement
Good metrics to mention if true in your background
Try to quantify any of these:
Practical Next Moves for the Dublin Market
- Apply by title cluster, not one title only
- Tailor CV keywords to each cluster
- For each role, mirror 5-8 exact keywords from the description
- Build one-page portfolio links or PDF samples:
-   €55k–€68k   is strongest for mid-level analyst/specialist roles with visible analytics and CRM capability
- If a role is more support-ops-heavy, offers may sit closer to the lower half
- If you can demonstrate reporting ownership, process design, and stakeholder partnership, you can credibly target the upper half
